title: Nessa and the Wobbling Rabbit
markdown:
High up in the Misty Crags, where the clouds tickle the very tops of the tallest friendliest pine trees, lived a young witch named Nessa. She had eyes as bright and curious as a pair of well-polished blueberries and hair the colour of warm comforting honey. Nessa loved her cosy cottage, a snug little home tucked away like a secret. It was always filled with the gentle bubbling of her special cauldrons. Her shelves were full of spell books. The pages smelled like old parchment mixed with the sweet scent of wild thyme. Sometimes her spells were as perfect and neat as little dancing fireflies. Other times they were a little bit wobbly, like jelly on a plate trying its best not to fall over.

One evening, as the sky began to blush with pinks, oranges, and soft purples, Nessa was practising a spell. She wanted to make her sleepy-time tea extra, wonderfully warm. She held her breath, whispered the special words, and waited. Instead of a gentle comforting warmth settling into her teacup, the teacup lifted itself right off the table and began to do a little unexpected jig. “Oh dear,” mumbled Nessa, and her cheeks turned a faint pretty pink. She was trying ever so hard to be a good witch, a proper witch. But her magic sometimes seemed to have a mind of its very own. A playful, silly mind.

As Nessa carefully tidied up her teacup — which had finally decided to settle down — she heard a tiny soft sound from just outside her little cottage door. It was a delicate sound, like a very small whisper of sadness. Sniffle. Sniffle. Nessa, with her blueberry-bright eyes, peeked out. Her nose twitched like a curious kitten. And there, huddled beside a patch of cheerful moon-daisies, was a little rabbit. It was the fluffiest rabbit Nessa had ever seen. Its ears were like velvety petals unfurling in the sun. And its whiskers wobbled with every single tiny breath it took. This little rabbit looked very, very lost, like a little puff of fluff that had blown too far from its home.

“Oh, you poor dear thing,” Nessa whispered, her heart giving a gentle sympathetic squeeze. The rabbit just looked up at her with big round wondering eyes. Its little nose wiggled ever so slightly. “Are you all alone out here?” Nessa asked softly. The rabbit gave a tiny sad little squeak. And then Nessa thought: the sky is turning a deep dusky blue. It’s getting dark. Should I really try to help him? She knew her own cottage was safe and warm. But this little rabbit needed to find its home. “Don’t worry, little one,” Nessa said, her voice firm and kind. “I will help you find your way.”

She gently scooped up the fluffy creature, who surprisingly snuggled right into her arms as if he’d known her forever. “I think,” Nessa decided, a little smile playing on her lips, “I shall call you Pipkin.” And at the sound of his new name, Pipkin’s whiskers gave a happy excited little twitch. “Now, Pipkin,” Nessa said, picking up her small well-loved spell book — the one with the worn leather cover and the slightly crooked clasp — “we must find your family.” Sometimes she felt a tiny bit worried herself, wondering if her magic was really good enough. But seeing Pipkin trust her completely, nestled safely in her arms, made her feel a tiny bit braver.

And so, with Pipkin nestled safely in her arms, a warm weight of fluffy trust, Nessa stepped out from her cosy cottage and into the whispering pines. The trees were tall and so very elegant. Their needles rustled with sounds that sounded like secrets being shared on the breeze. The path ahead still glowed softly with the last lingering rays of daylight. “Hoo-hoo, hello there, young witch,” a voice boomed, surprisingly cheerful and loud. And wouldn’t you know it, just around a bend in the path, stood a wizard. He had a long grey beard that seemed to trail all the way down to the forest floor. He wore spectacles that looked as if they were made of polished sparkling pebbles. But the most amusing thing about him was the maps. Oh, the maps. There were stacks and stacks of them, tumbling out of his pockets, tied with sturdy string, and even balanced on the very tip of his tall pointed hat.

“Good evening, Professor,” called Nessa, her voice bright. “Excuse me, Professor, have you by any chance seen a rabbit’s burrow around here? Pipkin here seems to have lost his home.” The wizard blinked. His pebble-spectacles slid down his nose. He adjusted them with a grunt and then began to rustle through his enormous collection of maps. “A rabbit, you say? Let me see now… Is it perhaps near the Glimmering Stream? Or perhaps the Whispering Waterfall? I have a map for both, you know, very detailed ones. And this one here,” he declared, unfurling a map so vast it nearly covered the entire path, “the Great Mushroom Forest map, might be precisely what you need.” Pipkin, nestled in Nessa’s arms, let out a little wiggle. His whiskers wobbled with silent giggles. “Thank you kindly, Professor,” Nessa said, still sweet and polite, though she knew the map was probably for a forest filled with giants, not rabbits. “But I don’t think those are quite the right maps for us today.”

As they continued their journey, a friendly little glow-worm, who was very busy lighting up a particularly dewy and intricate spiderweb, winked at them with its soft yellow light. “Lost, are we?” it buzzed softly, its light pulsing gently. “Don’t you worry. Follow me, just a little way. I think I saw a family of rabbits scampering towards the Hollow Tree just a little while ago. They looked a bit worried, like they were searching for someone.” Nessa’s heart leaped with a hopeful flutter. “Oh, thank you, little glow-worm. You are so very kind.”

They followed the glow-worm’s gentle guiding light. Soon they reached the edge of a part of the woods known as the Whispering Woods. It looked a little darker here. The trees seemed to lean in closer. The air grew cool on Nessa’s cheeks. A soft damp mist began to curl around their feet. It smelled faintly of wet earth and pine needles. Nessa looked down at Pipkin. He was still snuggled close, a warm bundle in her arms. But his whiskers seemed to be wobbling a little more nervously now. Nessa’s shoulders slumped. Her little spell book, usually a source of comfort, felt suddenly heavy in her hands. She had promised to help Pipkin, and now they were still lost.

Nessa sat down on a soft spongy patch of moss, and Pipkin, sensing her mood, settled himself in her lap. He nudged her hand gently with his wet cool nose. His little body felt warm and wonderfully grounding against her. Nessa looked down at her spell book, its pages filled with curious ancient symbols. She had tried so hard to do a complicated impressive spell earlier, but maybe a simple spell was what was needed now. A very old, very simple kind of magic. What if she used a finding spell?

She took a deep steadying breath and opened her book to a page with a little drawing of a compass, its needle pointing true. She closed her eyes, picturing Pipkin’s cosy burrow, his family waiting with open paws. She whispered the words, her voice soft but clear, like the gentle hum of a sleepy bee: “Little friend, lost and small, show us the way to home for all.” She didn’t expect a grand display, not really. But she had to try.

And then a tiny shimmering arrow appeared, right on the open page of her spell book. It glowed with a soft gentle inviting light, pointing steadfastly to the right. Nessa gasped, a sound of pure wonder. It worked. Pipkin’s whiskers twitched with pure excitement, a flurry of happy wobbles. “Come on, Pipkin,” Nessa said, her voice brimming with joy and relief. Following the glowing arrow, they hurried through the trees. The mist seemed to magically clear, and the path ahead became wonderfully brighter. And there, nestled beneath the roots of a grand old oak tree, was a snug little burrow, with a warm inviting light spilling from its entrance like a welcoming smile.

Suddenly, as if by magic, a group of rabbits tumbled out, their noses twitching with immense relief. “Pipkin. Oh, Pipkin, you’re back. We were so worried.” They gathered around him, nuzzling him with joyous hops and happy squeaks. Pipkin wriggled with delight, his whiskers a blur of happy wobbles. He turned and gave Nessa a grateful little nudge. “Thank you, dear Nessa,” chirped a motherly rabbit. “You brought our little Pipkin home safe and sound.” Nessa beamed. Her magic, for once, had been perfectly, wonderfully perfect.

Back in her own cosy cottage, with the fire crackling merrily and her teacup now wonderfully, perfectly warm, Nessa snuggled deep into her favourite armchair. She held her spell book close. The teacup stayed on the table. Pipkin’s whiskers, if she pictured them, still wobbled. The finding spell had been the simple one, which was how you knew a jigging cup could still point a rabbit home.
characters: Nessa (young witch of the Misty Crags), Pipkin (a fluffy wobbling rabbit)
author: StoryGen Community
